notes:
Account snapshot: mid-size fintech offering trade execution analytics + conversational assistant for advisors. Primary goal is deterministic inference cost and latency for regulated workflows.

PIecemeal notes from calls: 
- Customer requires reserved GPU pools with explicit throughput guarantees (TPS) and a documented failover headroom plan across regions/AZs.
- Target latency SLOs: 90ms p50, 150ms p95 for chat paths; reranking pipeline target p95 under 200ms.
- They want a 2-region primary/secondary deployment (us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 secondary) with autoscale/burst to hosted for >100% traffic spikes.
- Initial sizing ask: support steady-state 60 TPS and 120 TPS peak with 25% failover headroom -> rough reserved pool request: 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs primary, 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs secondary (customer numbers, needs Redwood sizing validation).
- Headroom policy preference: maintain 20-30% reserved headroom per region, with synchronous cross-region routing fallback and an async degraded-mode that disables non-critical reranking to preserve latency SLO.
- Cost sensitivity: high—financial modeling required to compare Dedicated reserved vs. Dedicated + burst to hosted. Customer asked for per-token cost projection.
- Security/compliance: mandatory KMS with BYOK, audit log retention 2 years, data residency for EU-origin requests to stay in eu-west-1 when possible.
- SLA negotiation points: include explicit throughput (TPS) guarantees during business hours, defined failover RTO (5 min detection + 15 min warmup) and credits tied to missed throughput SLOs.
- Short quotes: 'We need predictable capacity when markets open — spikes are sharp and regressions are costly.' — Head of Platform.

Documentation stubs: drive links above, Fireflies meeting for 2/17. Action items below.
sla_requirements: Throughput guarantee: baseline 60 TPS sustained; burst to 120 TPS for 15 min windows. RTO target for region failover: 20 minutes end-to-end. Credits: tiered if >10% time below throughput SLO in a 30-day window.
reserved_pool_plan: Proposal draft: us-east-1 primary: 16 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (supporting ~70-80 TPS steady with batching + KV cache). eu-west-1 secondary: 8 x reserved GPUs (+2 hot spares). Regional distribution accounts for 25% headroom. Autoscale policy: soft autoscale to burst using dedicated spare capacity for up to 2x baseline, hard fallback to hosted API for sustained >2x spikes.
failover_playbook_summary: Detection: infra tracing + synthetic p95 probes. Failover path: 1) route traffic to secondary region, 2) enable cached KV routing and reduced-request batching, 3) disable non-essential reranks. Expected warmup: 10-20 minutes depending on KV priming. Customer accepts warmup during market open but requests a warmup run before go-live.
poc_notes: POC scope: replay 7 days of production traffic (anonymized), validate p95 latency under dedicated pools, run coordinated multi-AZ failure (AZ outage simulation), measure effective headroom and tail latencies. Deliverables: capacity model, cost model, SLA draft with throughput clauses, failover runbook.
